relations.note: Kaśyapa fathers Śeṣa and the other nāgas through Kadrū.
Śeṣa is born among Kadrū’s immense brood of serpent sons.

relations.myth: Śeṣa repudiates his serpent family’s malice
relations.note: Śeṣa abandons his mother’s malicious serpent offspring and undertakes austerities.
Vinatā is Śeṣa’s half-aunt or stepmother through Kaśyapa.
Garuḍa is Śeṣa’s half-brother, born to Kaśyapa and Vinatā.

relations.myth: Garuḍa assists Śeṣa in bearing the world
relations.note: Brahmā appoints Garuḍa as Śeṣa’s helper in supporting the world.
Vāsuki is one of Śeṣa’s named nāga brothers.

relations.myth: Nāgas receive Balarāma’s returning serpent essence
relations.note: Vāsuki receives the thousand-headed serpent emerging from Balarāma at death.
Takṣaka is one of Śeṣa’s named nāga brothers.

relations.myth: Nāgas receive Balarāma’s returning serpent essence
relations.note: Takṣaka receives the thousand-headed serpent emerging from Balarāma at death.
Karkoṭaka is one of Śeṣa’s named nāga brothers.

relations.myth: Nāgas receive Balarāma’s returning serpent essence
relations.note: Karkoṭaka receives the thousand-headed serpent emerging from Balarāma at death.

relations.myth: Brahmā rewards Śeṣa’s austerities
relations.note: Brahmā grants Śeṣa the moral firmness he requests after his austerities.

relations.myth: Brahmā commissions Śeṣa to stabilize earth
relations.note: Śeṣa accepts Brahmā’s commission and bears the unstable earth.

relations.myth: Lotus-born Brahmā appears above reclining Viṣṇu
relations.note: Śeṣa supports Viṣṇu while Brahmā emerges upon the navel-born lotus.

relations.myth: Śeṣa enters below and bears the earth
relations.note: Śeṣa physically supports and stabilizes the personified earth.

relations.myth: Kṛṣṇa declares himself Ananta among nāgas
relations.note: Kṛṣṇa includes Ananta among his pre-eminent divine manifestations.

relations.myth: Śeṣa descends as Kṛṣṇa’s elder brother
relations.note: As Balarāma, Śeṣa becomes Kṛṣṇa’s elder brother and attendant expansion.

relations.myth: Viṣṇu reclines upon Śeṣa during cosmic suspension
relations.note: Śeṣa forms Viṣṇu’s couch and canopy upon the cosmic ocean.
Vaiṣṇava systems classify Śeṣa as Viṣṇu’s power, manifestation, or expansion.
Pāñcarātra and Purāṇic systems identify or closely coordinate Ananta with Saṅkarṣaṇa.

relations.myth: Balarāma returns to thousand-headed serpent form
relations.note: A white thousand-headed serpent leaves Balarāma’s mouth and enters the ocean.

relations.myth: Yogamāyā transfers the Śeṣa embryo
relations.note: Yogamāyā moves the embryo called Śeṣa from Devakī into Rohiṇī.

relations.myth: Yoganidrā awakens Viṣṇu upon Śeṣa
relations.note: The goddess withdraws from sleeping Viṣṇu while Śeṣa supports the developed cosmic scene.

relations.myth: Śeṣa embryo first resides in Devakī
relations.note: In his Balarāma incarnation, Śeṣa initially gestates within Devakī.

relations.myth: Transferred Śeṣa embryo becomes Balarāma
relations.note: Rohiṇī receives the transferred embryo and gives birth to Balarāma.

relations.myth: Lakṣmī attends Viṣṇu upon Śeṣa
relations.note: Lakṣmī attends reclining Viṣṇu’s feet above Śeṣa’s supporting coils.

relations.myth: Madhu threatens the Anantaśayana creation scene
relations.note: Madhu threatens Brahmā or confronts divine weapons beneath Viṣṇu and Śeṣa.

relations.myth: Kaiṭabha threatens the Anantaśayana creation scene
relations.note: Kaiṭabha threatens Brahmā or confronts divine weapons beneath Viṣṇu and Śeṣa.

relations.myth: Rudra emerges from Śeṣa’s apocalyptic fire
relations.note: Fire issuing from Śeṣa’s mouths assumes Rudra’s form and consumes the worlds.

relations.myth: Vāruṇī attends subterranean Śeṣa
relations.note: Vāruṇī accompanies Śeṣa in the Purāṇic description of his subterranean realm.

relations.myth: Vāruṇī supplies Balarāma divine liquor
relations.note: Vāruṇī provides divine liquor for Śeṣa’s incarnation Balarāma.

relations.myth: Varuṇa receives Balarāma’s serpent essence
relations.note: Varuṇa welcomes and worships the serpent issuing from Balarāma at death.

relations.myth: Varuṇa sends Vāruṇī to Balarāma
relations.note: Varuṇa sends Vāruṇī and her divine liquor for Balarāma’s enjoyment.

relations.myth: Ocean receives Balarāma’s serpent essence
relations.note: Personified Ocean receives the thousand-headed serpent returning from Balarāma.

relations.myth: Balarāma drags the disobedient Yamunā
relations.note: Balarāma drags Yamunā with his plough until she submits to his summons.

relations.myth: Yamunā submits and gives Balarāma gifts
relations.note: After submitting to Balarāma, Yamunā presents him with gifts.

relations.myth: Śeṣa incarnates as the sage Patañjali
relations.note: Medieval Chidambaram tradition makes Patañjali a serpent manifestation of Śeṣa.

relations.myth: Patañjali worships Śiva at Chidambaram
relations.note: As Patañjali, Śeṣa worships Śiva and receives a vision of his dance.

relations.myth: Patañjali and Vyāghrapāda witness Śiva’s dance
relations.note: Vyāghrapāda joins Śeṣa’s Patañjali incarnation in worship and witnessing the dance.

relations.myth: Śeṣa descends as Rāma’s younger brother
relations.note: Later Vaiṣṇava tradition identifies Lakṣmaṇa’s devoted service as Śeṣa’s incarnation.

relations.myth: Lakṣmaṇa attends Rāma through exile and war
relations.note: As Lakṣmaṇa, Śeṣa provides lifelong attendance and support to Rāma.

relations.myth: Lakṣmaṇa serves Sītā during Rāma’s exile
relations.note: Later theology interprets Lakṣmaṇa’s attendance upon Sītā as Śeṣa’s incarnate service.

relations.myth: Ananta becomes Pradyumna’s charioteer
relations.note: The thousand-headed Ananta serves Pradyumna as his charioteer.
Śrī Vaiṣṇava hagiography understands Rāmānuja as an incarnation of Ādiśeṣa.
Certain lineage traditions identify Maṇavāḷa Māmunikaḷ with Śeṣa’s continuing incarnational service.
